find_place.description: Search Diyanet's directory by name and get back the district id the other steps need. The step to put in front of them when all a workflow has is a place name out of a form field. Turkish letters and accents are matched for you - 'corlu' finds ÇORLU and 'basaksehir' finds BAŞAKŞEHİR - which the service's own search does not do. A single match comes back with its city and country named, so you can see it is the right one; several matches come back as a list rather than a guess. No API key required.
find_place.name: find_place

parameters.description: The place to search for. Part of a name is enough: 'kahraman' finds KAHRAMANMARAŞ.
parameters.name: query

parameters.description: Which level of the directory to search. Districts are what prayer times are keyed on.
parameters.name: place_type

parameters.description: Narrow the search to one country, by name or id. Leave empty to search them all.
parameters.name: country

get_next_prayer.description: Get the next prayer due at a place and how long there is until it - the step a reminder is built on: 'Akşam in 20 minutes'. Sunrise is skipped, because it is published alongside the prayers but is not one, and after Yatsı the answer rolls over to tomorrow's İmsak rather than running out at midnight. Today's full timetable comes back with it. No API key required.
get_next_prayer.name: get_next_prayer

parameters.description: The country, by name or by id. Diyanet publishes for Turkey and for cities in many other countries. Defaults to Türkiye.
parameters.name: country

parameters.description: The city (il), by name or by id - İSTANBUL, KONYA, 539. Defaults to İstanbul. Turkish letters and accents are matched for you, so 'istanbul' finds İSTANBUL.
parameters.name: city

parameters.description: The district (ilçe), by name or by id. This is what the timetable is keyed on: times differ by a few minutes between districts of the same city. Defaults to İSTANBUL, the district covering the city itself. A district id makes the step skip the two lookups above it, so it is the fastest thing to pass in from an earlier step.
parameters.name: district

parameters.description: The zone to read these times in, as an IANA name. Diyanet publishes clock times with no zone attached, so this is what turns them into moments a reminder can be scheduled from, and what 'today' and 'now' mean. Leave it on Europe/Istanbul unless the district is somewhere else - Europe/Berlin for the German ones, for instance.
parameters.name: timezone

get_place.description: Look up one country, city or district by its id, with the levels above it named. The step to put in front of a condition when an id arrived from outside the workflow and ought to be checked before a timetable is read from it. No API key required.
get_place.name: get_place

parameters.description: The id to look up, as it came from 'Find a place' or one of the listing steps.
parameters.name: place_id

parameters.description: Which level of the directory the id belongs to.

get_prayer_times.description: Get a day's prayer times for a Turkish district as the Directorate of Religious Affairs publishes them - the times the local mosques actually call to. All six come back: İmsak (Fajr), Güneş (sunrise), Öğle (Dhuhr), İkindi (Asr), Akşam (Maghrib, which is iftar) and Yatsı (Isha), each named in Turkish and English, each as a clock time and as a full timestamp a reminder can be scheduled from. The day's Hijri date and the length of its fast come with them. Name the place by district, or leave it on İstanbul; leave the date empty for today. No API key required.

get_prayer_times_range.description: Get a stretch of the timetable - a week, a month, a year, or exactly the days between two dates - for a calendar, a digest or a loop. Note that 'monthly' and 'yearly' are the service's own periods and mean the whole calendar month or year the start date falls in, so a month from the 16th answers from the 1st; use 'range' for exactly the days you name. Every result reports the span it actually covers. Answers longer than a page are followed and stitched together, so a year comes back whole rather than as its first hundred days. No API key required.

get_ramadan_timetable.description: Get the imsakiye: every fast of Ramadan for one district, with its sahur (İmsak) and iftar (Akşam) times, the length of each fast, and which day of Ramadan it is. Ramadan is a Hijri month, so it is found by reading the Hijri date on each day rather than by calendar arithmetic - and when it straddles New Year, as it will at the end of this decade, the neighbouring year is fetched so the timetable comes back whole. The longest and shortest fasts of the month come with it. No API key required.

description: Prayer times as the Turkish Directorate of Religious Affairs (Diyanet İşleri Başkanlığı) publishes them, for about nine hundred districts across Turkey and Northern Cyprus and for Turkish communities abroad. These are the printed-imsakiye times the local mosques call to rather than a calculation, so a reminder built on them agrees with the neighbourhood. Get a day's six times - İmsak, Güneş, Öğle, İkindi, Akşam and Yatsı - named in Turkish and English and stamped with a time zone so a reminder can be scheduled straight off them; get the next prayer and the minutes until it; pull a week, a month or a whole year in one step; and get the Ramadan imsakiye itself, with sahur, iftar and the length of every fast. Places are found by name as well as by id, with Turkish letters matched for you so 'corlu' finds ÇORLU, and the country-city-district hierarchy is walked for you rather than left as three lookup steps. Paged answers are stitched back together, so a year comes back whole. No account or API key required.
